properties.title: TiO₂ Abundance · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Clementine UVVIS DIM Mosaic (5 bands: 415, 750, 900, 950, 1000 nm, 100 m/pixel) combined with OMAT as a 6-element input vector. 1D CNN: two Conv1D layers (32 filters, kernel=2, ReLU), MaxPooling1D (pool=2), Dense(64, ReLU), single linear output. L2 regularization (0.001) on all layers. Adam optimizer (lr=0.01), max 400 epochs, early stopping (patience=30), z-score normalization. Trained on 49 ground-truth points from Apollo, Luna, and Chang'E missions including Chang'E-6. Chang'E-6 samples (TiO₂: 2.7 wt%) corrected a systematic overestimation of TiO₂ in lunar maria by the equation model. R²=0.96+ on training set; LOOCV R²=0.831.
properties.lri:data_use_note: High-resolution TiO₂ abundance at 100 m/pixel — key proxy for ilmenite (FeTiO₃) concentration. Combined with FeO, identifies ilmenite-rich zones for oxygen and titanium extraction. CNN model corrects prior overestimation of high-TiO₂ basalts: the classical equation placed high-TiO₂ material (>9 wt%) widely across Oceanus Procellarum and Mare Tranquillitatis; the CNN constrains it to the northern and SW parts of Mare Tranquillitatis, consistent with LP GRS (which detected no pixels above 9 wt% globally except 1-2 in Mare Tranquillitatis at 7.9-8.0 wt%).
properties.lri:quality_note_short: 1D CNN inversion from Clementine UVVIS, calibrated with Chang'E-6 samples. LOOCV R²=0.831. Global mean 0.99 wt%; maria 2.66 wt%. CNN corrects prior overestimation of high-TiO₂ basalts; high-TiO₂ material correctly concentrated in northern/SW Mare Tranquillitatis, consistent with LP GRS.
properties.lri:quality_note: TiO₂ abundance derived from 1D CNN inversion of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). The addition of Chang'E-6 samples (TiO₂: 2.7 wt%, a low-Ti farside mare) had the largest calibration impact of any sample on the TiO₂ model — the sample deviated ~3.0 wt% from the previously fitted line, greater than the RMSE of 1.24 wt%, correcting a systematic overestimation of TiO₂ in maria. LOOCV R²=0.831. Global mean 0.99 wt%, unimodal continuous distribution, mode 0.42 wt%. CNN TiO₂ is ~0.21 wt% lower globally and ~1.04 wt% lower in maria compared to the companion equation model. The key improvement is spatial: the equation model placed high-TiO₂ basalts (>9 wt%) widely across Oceanus Procellarum and Mare Tranquillitatis; the CNN concentrates them in the northern and SW parts of Mare Tranquillitatis — consistent with LP GRS (no signals >9 wt% globally, 7.9-8.0 wt% in 1-2 pixels of Mare Tranquillitatis) and Apollo 11/17 sample TiO₂ measurements. Oceanus Procellarum TiO₂ is revised to ~4 wt% (down from >9 wt% in the equation model). Key limitation: LOOCV R² of 0.831 is the second-lowest among the five oxides; TiO₂ inversion from optical data is inherently more uncertain than FeO. Additional farside mare samples are needed to fully constrain the nearside-farside TiO₂ dichotomy.
